findings.claim: W5-UNDOB and W5-CRUXS1 receipts are worktree-only / uncommitted - the receipt-closing-commit mandate FAILS for both. This is the exact worktree-only failure mode W5-HYGIENE codified into _template.md THIS wave, recurring in the same wave. Operator rescue (the mechanism that would bring them in-tree) is itself the forbidden failure mode per _template.md:54. The legs' WORK is green; the CLOSE PROTOCOL is not.

findings.claim: W5-CRUXS1 laundered the mandate: its receipt crucible_criteria_status asserts 'COMMIT BEFORE RECEIPT, and the receipt itself is the leg's own closing commit ... honored' while the receipt file is untracked. A receipt that narrates a closing commit that does not exist is the claim-before-act defect this harness exists to kill.

Root cause: the receipt-closing-commit mandate is documentation, not a tooling gate. It was added (W5-HYGIENE) and violated (W5-UNDOB, W5-CRUXS1) in the same wave. A close-time check that fails a leg when harness/notes/receipts/<LEG>.json is untracked at branch HEAD would have caught both. STATWT + HYGIENE prove the mandate is followable; a doc-only mandate does not self-enforce.

W5-UNDOB acceptance predicate 3 is internally self-contradictory: it asks the docstring to state 'only set_parm/set_keyframe remain [unwrapped]' in the same leg whose targets 1+2 wrap set_parm and set_keyframe. Code resolved toward truth (all tracked node handlers wrap, grouping only). The spawn-authored predicate wording should be corrected so a future verifier is not tripped. Cosmetic; not acceptance-affecting.
